Village you've been walking held the center of this city's lesbian and gay life for more than a hundred years.","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Willa Cather signed her college letters 'William,' lived with Edith Lewis for nearly forty years, and burned most of her correspondence before she died in 1947.","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Audre Lorde found her own refuge at the Bagatelle on University Place, where, she wrote in Zami, 'the Bag was always The Club.'","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":4},{"text":"In 1892, a vice cop walked into a club on this street and left disgusted, filing a report on the waiters — 'men of degenerate type,' he wrote, some 'rouging their necks,' who sang 'filthy ditties' in falsetto and dropped uninvited into any visitor's chair.","source_id":"ccc6937c-b947-4386-9327-1b88def518a3","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"The place was the Slide, a drag club an entrepreneur had opened in the early 1890s at 157 Bleecker Street, in the building that now houses Kenny's Castaways.","source_id":"ccc6937c-b947-4386-9327-1b88def518a3","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4,"also_cites":["92d9b581-ee91-414d-8b18-a912efa016c8"]},{"text":"By then the whole Lower East Side had a name for scandalous 'resorts' — dancing halls, saloons and brothels where the city's 'inverts' and 'fairies' gathered for cross-dressing spectaculars, dancing, and back-room encounters.","source_id":"92d9b581-ee91-414d-8b18-a912efa016c8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Bleecker was notorious, second only to the Bowery for its rough and racy reputation, with Greene and Mercer Streets among the busiest red-light districts in the city.","source_id":"ccc6937c-b947-4386-9327-1b88def518a3","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Places like the Slide, or Columbia Hall — better known as Paresis Hall, at 392 Bowery — did a strange double duty: straight thrill-seekers came to gape and closeted middle-class men came for a secret thrill, yet they were also genuine centers of gay male social life and relatively safe places to gather.","source_id":"ccc6937c-b947-4386-9327-1b88def518a3","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4,"also_cites":["92d9b581-ee91-414d-8b18-a912efa016c8"]},{"text":"For curious straights it was a stop on the voyeuristic 'slumming tours,' and detectives would steer out-of-towners hunting 'the low life' to the Slide first, as the New York Herald reported that same year.","source_id":"ccc6937c-b947-4386-9327-1b88def518a3","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4,"also_cites":["92d9b581-ee91-414d-8b18-a912efa016c8"]},{"text":"The police shut the Slide down in 1892.","source_id":"ccc6937c-b947-4386-9327-1b88def518a3","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Down the block at 183 Bleecker Street, a sex club called the Black Rabbit, with gay-themed acts, held on until a police raid finally closed it in 1900.","source_id":"ccc6937c-b947-4386-9327-1b88def518a3","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Half a century later, a different kind of hidden life was being lived just up the street.","source_id":"faddd103-af53-42b5-aaed-182c62785acd","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"No. 337 Bleecker was the home of Lorraine Hansberry, whose A Raisin in the Sun opened on Broadway in 1959 and put a Black family's life on the American stage like nothing before it.","source_id":"faddd103-af53-42b5-aaed-182c62785acd","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"It ran two years, and made her the first Black playwright to win the New York Drama Critics Circle Award for Best Play of the year.","source_id":"faddd103-af53-42b5-aaed-182c62785acd","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"What almost no one knew was that through the 1950s she was quietly writing anonymous letters to One magazine and The Ladder, early gay-rights publications, while married to Robert Nemiroff, who knew she was a lesbian — the two divorced in 1964 but stayed close.","source_id":"faddd103-af53-42b5-aaed-182c62785acd","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"One last thing before we finish, and you'll smell it before I name it.","source_id":"fb2522af-aef1-4e12-9466-31fbf102959a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"This is the most aromatic stretch of the whole tour — home to the fabulous Murray's Cheese and to Faicco's Italian Specialties, run by the same family since 1900 and selling what the book swears is the best sopressata in the United States.","source_id":"fb2522af-aef1-4e12-9466-31fbf102959a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"And that closes the loop, back where we started.","source_id":"GLUE_CLOSING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Thank you for coming along with me today. When you're ready, take your time to keep exploring on your own.","source_id":"GLUE_CLOSING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":4}]}
